title: Use the slope formula
text: Since $$x=r cos\left(\theta\right)$$ and $$y=r sin\left(\theta\right)$$, the slope is $$\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{r'\sin\theta+r\cos\theta}{r'\cos\theta-r\sin\theta}$$

title: Plug in
text: At $$\theta=\frac{\pi}{2}$$, $$r=\frac{\pi}{2}$$ and $$r'=1$$. Then $$r' sin\left(\theta\right)+r cos\left(\theta\right)=1$$ and $$r' cos\left(\theta\right)-r sin\left(\theta\right)=\frac{-\pi}{2}$$, so the slope is $$\frac{-2}{\pi}$$.
